reasoning: The application implements the spec goals: view.js wires a click listener (initializeFaceTapHighlighting) that calls clearHighlights() then highlightFace(faceId), adding the .highlighted class and painting #faceCanvas, and updateCanvasSize redraws the remembered face after a resize. The mouse-driven face-hover spec exercises the same highlightFace path and passes, confirming drawing/class logic works. The two failures are confined to withTouchContext + locator.tap(). The thumbnail also has inline onmouseenter/onmouseleave handlers, and the emulated touch tap produces those mouse compatibility events (the very events the spec says a touch screen never fires). That makes the tap-set highlight transient: mouseenter paints/classes, then a trailing mouseleave calls clearHighlights() and wipes the canvas and class. Test 1's toHaveClass missed the transient entirely (received 'face-thumbnail'), while test 2's class assertion caught the transient but the subsequent canvas pixel read ran after the clear, so faceOverlayIsPainted was false. Because the app's click-based tap path and resize redraw are present and correct, the spec goals are achievable with the running application; the test is wrong in relying on an emulated tap that does not leave the click-handler highlight set.
affectedTests: Photo Details - Responsive › photo_details_face_highlight_works_with_a_coarse_pointer - tapping a face draws its box
Photo Details - Responsive › photo_details_face_highlight_survives_rotation - resizing redraws the box instead of losing it
suggestedAction: Fix the test's coarse-pointer simulation rather than the app. Drive the thumbnail's click path deterministically (e.g. dispatch/click through the element so the app's click listener runs and its highlight persists) or adjust withTouchContext so the tap does not inject the spurious mouseenter/mouseleave hover-emulation events (for example, keep hasTouch but avoid isMobile hover emulation). Then assert the persistent post-tap state: thumbnail has .highlighted, faceOverlayIsPainted is true, and after resize/rotation the highlight is redrawn. Preserve the existing spec coverage and assertions; do not weaken them or skip the tests.
